# `Q-26-9` — lmd autoload failed

> A module listed under `lmd: modules:` (in `_quarto.yml` or the front matter) could not be loaded before the document's first cell, or the entry is not a module name or a one-key `global: module` map. The document's lmd cells are left as written.

## What this means

`lmd: modules:` names modules to `require` before a document's first lmd
cell runs, each bound to a global so every cell can use it without its
own `require`:

```yaml
lmd:
  modules:
    - components/cards        # binds `cards`
    - ui: components/widgets  # binds `ui`
```

One of the entries failed. The error is located on the entry, and
because the cells of the page were written against the modules the
entry promised, none of them runs: each is left displayed as code, the
way a cell with an error is. A broken prelude fails the page once, not
once per cell.

## Why this happens

- The module was not found where `require` looks: next to the
  document, at the project root with a leading `/`, or in an extension
  addressed by its name (`cards/deck` for `_extensions/cards/deck.lmd`).
- The module did not compile ([`Q-26-8`](Q-26-8.qmd)) or raised while
  loading; the message names the module file and line.
- The entry is neither a string nor a one-key map, or the global it
  would bind is not a Lua name (`my-module`; write `mine: my-module`).

## How to fix

Fix the entry or the module it names. A string entry binds the last
segment of the module name (`components/cards` binds `cards`); when that
is not a valid or convenient name, use the map form to choose one.

## Related errors

- [`Q-26-8`](Q-26-8.qmd): the module compiled badly.
- [`Q-26-4`](Q-26-4.qmd): a cell failed at run time; with autoload
  working, a cell that uses an unbound name reports this instead.
